REFLECTION.2_intent_check_identity_vs_salience_and_: The generic-AG preference (S_A +0.55) is real but SALIENCE-confounded (motif_gap 1.4 s.d.; the generic decoy is a weaker 3'SS) -- it is 'partner vs generic site', not identity. The salience-controlled REAL-acceptor arm is +0.616 [0.46,0.74] (n=30). Its distance confound (real decoys median +19.5nt farther) was ADJUDICATED: OLS S_A_real~signed_gap gives intercept(gap=0) +0.606 +-0.077, slope +0.00105/nt, corr +0.08 -- distance explains ~0.02 of the +0.62. The identity signal SURVIVES distance control: L3H1 prefers its intron-mate PARTNER over a non-partner real acceptor as a partner-IDENTITY effect, not distance-decay. The |gap|<=20 stratum (n=5) is +0.40 [0.07,0.75], consistent but underpowered. This is the novel, R15-safe result over the prior restore-at-position C9.

REFLECTION.4_c_address_read: L2H15 retains 89% of S_A when mean-ablated (removes only 11%), yet p=0.021 vs the 47-head layer-0-2 null -- a statistically real but MINOR contributor to the matched-decoy preference. The preference is built largely elsewhere/diffusely, distinct from L2H15's larger role vs the CORRUPT partner in l2_accounting (C9). Not claimed as 'L2H15 builds the address'; reported.
REFLECTION.5_escaped_failure_modes: The real-acceptor distance confound (the chief risk) was measured and adjudicated, not assumed. C-Redirect uses a no-relocation DiD baseline so its positivity is not a corruption artifact (the earlier W--W+ metric would have been). The R15-forced kv transplant is demoted to a reported guard so a 'super-additive recovery' cannot be mis-sold as content-addressing. The n=30 real-acc subset is modest power (reported). No number agrees to suspicious precision.
